newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks start lower before Buba meeting.
newsitem.headline: German stocks start lower before Buba meeting.

text.p: German shares got off to a listless start on Thursday, trading lower with dealers saying they were expecting no news to invigorate the sleepy pre-holiday market.
Even the Bundesbank's last council meeting of the year was expected to provide little stimulus.
Most analysts expect the central bank to leave German interest rates unchanged, although a decision about the bank's money supply growth target range for 1997 is expected.
The DAX index of 30 top German shares was down 8.06 points, or 0.29 percent, at 2,812.69 points by 1017 GMT.
Thursday is the last trading day for the December DAX futures contract and dealers said that could lead to some volatility in the day's dealings as players move to cover their futures positions.
The expiry of futures contracts on individual shares could also lead to volatility in stocks such as industrial group Daimler, electronics group Siemens and insurer Allianz AG.
"Because of the expiry we could see a few correctins on a few stocks," said one dealer.
Dealers said the market should be supported by strength on Wall Street and a firm dollar, but said that the DAX was likely to be trapped in a fairly narrow range.
"If the DAX goes above resistance at 2,825 points, it could rise to 2,850 and on the downside we are unlikely to drop below 2,800 points," said one dealer.

The day's most heavily traded stock was Commerzbank, Germany's third largest bank, which dropped 27 pfennigs to trade at 39.15 marks, erasing some of the gains it made in recent days on unconfirmed merger speculation.
